doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: State of jazz today and staying in St. Petersburg
summary: He feels jazz is blossoming and says persistence and drive matter more than talent.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well I really want to thank you for your time. We chatted for quite a long time here. What do you think of the state of jazz today?

Oh man it’s blooming all over the place. Blossoming. I love what I see. I mean you go on the Internet and you can get anything that you want. It’s all there. It’s beautiful. And © Fillius Jazz Archive -28-
more concerts, more everything. I have more gigs than I can handle. Don’t tell the guys up north now.
Right. That’s right. We don’t them all coming down here, right?

But you see, speaking of that, I had a choice between going — I could have gone anywhere. I could have gone to L.A. to try to do the studios thing, I could have gone to New York or gone anywhere. But I chose to come to a little place like St. Petersburg. And it has blossomed into a big thing. It’s like the old story about the mountain coming to Muhammad. That’s what happened. All you need is the concept, and work long and hard enough. Persistence. You don’t necessarily need a great deal of talent but you need the drive. The energy to get you where you’d like to go.
